I requested a quote for medication from the Vet Popular group pharmacy for pickup yesterday (October 9, 2026) at the Vila Carrão unit. The service was provided via WhatsApp by attendant Matheus Oliveira.
The attendant sent me the quote with the prices of the medications. The quote indicates a box of Simparic medication with 3 tablets. I picked it up as agreed last night, we went to give the medication to the pet and there was only one tablet inside the box, the medication was in the original box with the description of 3 units.

I contacted the company again via WhatsApp and was assisted by Aline Araújo, who told me that the closed box contains 3 tablets, which is why it appears that way in the system. But that the sale is for 1 unit at the price of 134.99, referring to one tablet. The attendant even informs me in conversation as if I had approved the value referring to only one tablet. But before, at the time of purchase, it was not informed and in the quote (print attached) it is shown as 1 box 3, that is, 3 tablets. By law, they cannot sell the product in fractional quantities in its original packaging, and the customer must be informed in the quote that the price refers to only 1 tablet.
As I informed the attendant, I expect at least a refund or the other 2 tablets.

We received excellent care; the veterinarian suggested an ultrasound, which diagnosed cystitis. She administered medication and advised us on the next steps. Professional and high-quality service.

I'm leaving this account to document a real experience my family went through and also to clarify some points regarding the clinic's response.

On September 30th, my sister-in-law took her dog, a Pinscher, to the Vet Popular Vila Carrão clinic to investigate a cough and slightly labored breathing. The intention was to find out what was happening to her.

During the appointment, three injectable medications were administered, including an antibiotic and furosemide. My sister-in-law has no technical knowledge about veterinary medications and trusted the staff's instructions.

After returning home, a few minutes later, the dog's condition worsened very rapidly; she began to faint and her tongue turned purple. Because of this, my sister-in-law immediately returned to the clinic with the dog in an attempt to save her. Unfortunately, she did not survive and passed away.

When I arrived at the clinic to help my sister-in-law, I found her alone in a room, crying desperately. She is diabetic and was feeling very unwell given the whole situation. I was the one who had to ask them to check her blood sugar. Later, when we got home, we also found that her blood pressure was very high.

Therefore, I consider it very important to clarify the clinic's statement about an alleged "invasion," aggression, intimidation, and use of foul language.

There was no invasion. There was no threat, aggression, or intention to intimidate any professional.

The people who arrived at the clinic were there to help my sister-in-law and try to understand what was happening to the dog. Everyone was naturally shaken, nervous, and desperate in the face of a situation where an animal was dying and an owner was in shock.

At no point, as far as we witnessed, were there any foul words or any aggression against the veterinarian. What existed was a family trying to get answers: we wanted to understand what had happened, what medications had been administered, why the puppy had deteriorated so quickly, and what could be done to save her.

What struck us most was precisely the lack of support at that moment. My sister-in-law was alone, crying uncontrollably, and our perception was that there was a lack of empathy and sensitivity towards a pet owner who had just experienced an extremely traumatic situation.

We were also very concerned by the assertion that the puppy had died because the owner hadn't authorized hospitalization.

Based on our experience, my sister-in-law didn't receive an explanation that made it clear there was such a serious and imminent risk. It wasn't explained to her that it would be necessary to remain in the unit to observe a possible reaction to the medications, nor that there was a risky situation requiring a different approach. A few minutes after leaving the consultation, the puppy's condition worsened dramatically, and she died.

I am not stating that the medications were the cause of death. The cause of death is still under investigation, and the body was sent for autopsy precisely to technically clarify what happened.

What we are questioning is the sequence of events, the instructions received, the assistance provided at that time, and the way a distressed pet owner was treated.

The clinic has the right to present its version. We also have the right to present ours.

We hope that the autopsy, medical records, and other technical elements will clarify the facts and allow us to understand exactly what happened.

A family lost a beloved animal. A pet owner went through an extremely traumatic situation. The least we expected at that moment was support, transparency, and answers.

I leave this account so that other pet owners pay attention, ask questions about the medications and procedures indicated, and make sure they understand their indications, risks, and instructions before authorizing them.

I am sharing this account as a warning so that pet owners are attentive and ask questions before authorizing any procedure or medication.
On September 30th, my sister-in-law took her dog, a Pinscher, to Vet Popular to investigate a cough accompanied by slightly labored breathing. Until then, she was fine and was taken precisely to find out the cause of these symptoms.
During the appointment, three injectable medications were prescribed and administered, including an antibiotic and furosemide. My sister-in-law was alone, had no technical knowledge about the medications, and trusted the professional guidance presented during the consultation.
After returning home, the dog became very ill, fainted, and her tongue turned purple. She was rushed back to the clinic, but unfortunately, she did not survive and passed away.

The cause of death is still being investigated. The body was sent for necropsy, and we will await the results to understand what really happened and if there is a relationship between the procedures performed and the death.

What causes us great concern is how quickly the condition worsened so severely after the initial treatment. The visit to the veterinarian was for a diagnostic consultation, where the dog was apparently out of danger. Therefore, I am sharing this account primarily as a warning to pet owners: before authorizing medication administration, try to understand exactly what is being given, what the indication is, the risks, and what alternatives exist.

A life was lost, and we hope that the investigation will clarify the facts. May other pet owners have enough information to make informed decisions when their animals are receiving treatment.

My dog ​​had two tests done today and it took more than an hour to be seen. All the other patients, who arrived after her, were seen. When I questioned the reception, I was informed that the veterinarian was on her lunch break. Seriously, and there wasn't anyone else to do the test? She hadn't urinated all day to have the sample taken, and she was extremely stressed by the delay. And then, when I was finally seen by the doctor, she complained that I was nervous and that's why the dog was nervous. It's very easy to say that when she wasn't the one who waited more than an hour to be seen, having to go to the hospital several times a week for tests. I found her very lacking in empathy and professionalism.

On the other days I went to the hospital, I didn't experience this.

My experience was quite negative, and since the clinic itself requested an evaluation, I thought it was fair to share what I went through.

I was at the Hospital Vet Popular Vila Carrão on September 13, 2026, when I took my cat with a case of blood in his urine. Initially, I was well attended to, especially by Dr. Denis. After the first ultrasound, hospitalization and urethral catheterization were indicated, which I agreed to and authorized, concerned exclusively with his recovery.

However, as the days passed, I began to have many doubts regarding the handling of the case. The information received by telephone was insufficient and, at times, contradictory, and the visiting hours made it even more difficult to closely monitor my cat's progress.

On September 15th, I was informed that he was progressing well and that they would attempt to remove the catheter to see if he could urinate on his own. The following day, during the visit, I was informed that he still hadn't urinated and that a new catheterization would be necessary, in addition to another 48 hours of hospitalization.

At that moment, I also noticed that he was in a dirty cage with a very small amount of the worst quality sand, along with a diaper, which worried me a lot. I informed them that I would not authorize a new catheterization without prior communication with me. Despite this, the following morning I was informed that he had been catheterized again during the night, without my authorization being requested or me even being notified beforehand.

Given this, and after speaking with the veterinarian who has been treating my cat since he was a kitten, I decided to remove him from the clinic. Up to that point, I had already spent more than R$ 3,000, but my decision was not motivated solely by financial reasons. The main reason was the loss of confidence in the handling of the case and in communication with the team.

I picked up my cat on September 17th, around 4 PM, and took him home to be monitored by my trusted veterinarian. As soon as he arrived, he ate, played, asked for affection, and a few minutes later, urinated spontaneously and without blood. Today, September 20th, he continues to progress well, urinating without a catheter, eating, and correctly following the prescribed medications.

I understand that there are cases where hospitalization is truly necessary, and I don't question the importance of veterinary care. My criticism is directed at the specific handling of the case, the communication with the owner, and, mainly, the performance of a procedure that I had expressly stated I did not authorize without prior communication.

My experience was very different from what I expected from a veterinary health service. I hope the administration uses this account to review protocols, communication with owners, hospitalization conditions, and the real need to prolong certain treatments when other monitoring options exist.

Unfortunately, it was an experience that completely shattered my confidence in the clinic, and for that reason, I do not intend to return.

We left with our hearts at peace and very grateful to have found professionals who truly demonstrate love for what they do. The care in every detail is noticeable, from the reception to the veterinary care.

The doctor who was treating her forgot to order the additional tests that were requested. I even had the dog admitted to the hospital, where she was sedated, but they canceled the surgery.

He was evaluated by a team and, after surgery, monitored by the inpatient team. I am grateful to the entire Vet Popular team for all their effort and dedication!

I spent quite a bit of time here, reading the comments before deciding to take my pet to the clinic. Now, I'm leaving my review here to support anyone who might be interested. Overall, I approve of the clinic and the service. The place is well-structured, clean, with on-site laboratory resources, which discourages external referrals for exams, which is very good. My pet was seen by Dr. Cassia, who was very attentive, cordial, and helpful. I will probably use the clinic's services again. The service at the cashier's window had two nuances; on the first day I went, a very attentive young man attended to us, always explaining everything: procedures, cashback system, exam protocols, etc. On the return visit, we were attended to by an apathetic and indifferent woman. I had to remind her about the cashback to use it; she gave us the exam referral and didn't even say what we should do to be seen, where to go, etc. Based on this, I believe that Vet Popular's proposal is great, but it lacks a bit of standardization in service. Overall, this is constructive criticism so that the management of the establishment does not allow it to be brought down to the lowest standard, as the clinic's potential is enormous.
